# NSPanel HAUI 0.5.4

0.5.4 makes a panel feel fast again and makes a failed display install say why. Opening a panel and paging inside it no longer crawl, a TFT install that fails names its reason within seconds instead of after twenty minutes, and `nspanel_haui.update_tft` fails with that reason instead of answering as if it had started.

The editor follows: the install picker sits with the versions it installs, the **Device inventory** header shows what is waiting as figures, and a display or firmware failure is spelled out where you pressed the button.

This release updates the integration, the editor and the firmware. Both TFTs are unchanged, so display version 0.4.5 remains required. The firmware carries the two changes a panel notices: the loop that paces display commands, and the upload events behind the fast failure report.

## Before updating

**The Display Model entity is a dropdown.** It is a `select` with **Landscape** and **Portrait** instead of a `0`/`1` number, so `number.<device>_display_model` becomes `select.<device>_display_model`. Point automations that set the model at the new entity; nothing has to be re-entered, because the hub writes the option on every connect and the editor's **Display Model** setting under **Device Settings → General** is unchanged. Upgrade the integration and the firmware together, so the entity and the hub agree ([upgrade notes](docs/user/update.md#display-model-is-a-dropdown)).

**`nspanel_haui.update_tft` raises instead of pretending.** A call that cannot start an install — no matching device, updates off, an install already running, an unusable URL — now fails with the hub's reason, and a call that starts answers with the update state (`started`, then `installing`, `done` or `error`). An automation that relied on the old silent success needs an error path or a `response_variable`; the editor's **Install** button shows the same reason in the **Updates** sidebar ([actions](docs/user/actions.md#nspanel_hauiupdate_tft)).

Install the firmware that ships with this version to get the faster rendering and the immediate failure report. A panel that stays on older firmware keeps working: it renders slower in the old way and a failed upload is only noticed when the install times out after 20 minutes. A custom build (`firmware_variant: custom`) never receives the released image; rebuild it from `esphome/install.yaml`.

## Changed

- **Faster page opens** — The **Page settle delay** default drops from `0.1` to `0.05` s, halving the wait between the display's page confirmation and the first command of the render. The confirmation already means the page is active, so the delay is only a margin. A device that already stores `0.1` keeps it until it is changed under **Screen** ([Device settings](docs/user/editor/device.md)).
- **Updates sidebar** — The install picker for a display or firmware update opens above the **Update settings** card, with the versions it installs, instead of at the sidebar's foot ([Updates](docs/user/update.md)).
- **Fleet header** — The **Device inventory** header shows pending updates and the integration version as toned figures in the diagnostics tiles' type — a green check when nothing is waiting, an amber download when one is, a warning tag while the panels disagree — so the value reads first without growing the strip ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).
- **Connection segments** — The segments at the foot of the Device inventory name their device and state in a popover on hover or focus instead of in the browser's own tooltip, which a keyboard could not reach ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).
- **Backups** — **Import** and **Copy to other devices** say what they replace in a warning banner instead of a line under the buttons ([Backups](docs/user/editor/README.md)).
- **Quieter log** — The hub logs each ESPHome command chunk at **Debug** instead of **Info**, so a ticking page no longer writes about a line per second into the Home Assistant log. Set the device's **Log level** to **Debug** when you need them.
- **Release process** — The release workflow now merges the release into `dev` and `dev` into `master` once it published, so both branches end on one commit instead of a manual merge-back ([Release process](docs/develop/release.md)).

## Fixed

- **A panel draws fast again** — Opening a panel and paging inside one took 1.8–2.5 s and 0.4–0.5 s. The Nextion component sends one command per ESPHome loop phase, and that phase was gated on the default 16 ms `loop_interval`, so `command_spacing: 2ms` was really ~16 ms per command. A full command queue then needed longer to drain than its 8 s stale age, so the tail of a heavy render was dropped unsent and left stale widgets on the page. The firmware runs the loop every 2 ms again and the configured spacing applies ([Nextion component](docs/develop/nextion.md#command-pacing-costs-one-component-phase-per-command)).
- **A TFT install that never started is no longer silent** — An install from a URL or a local file is followed like any other: it starts on a panel that has not handshaked yet instead of turning into a release install, a second request names the install that is still running and when it started, and `nspanel_haui.update_tft` raises with the hub's reason and answers with the update state.
- **A failed upload is reported in seconds** — The firmware sends the reason it could not install (no network, the server's answer, a refused display) as soon as the upload ends, so the install fails in the sidebar and on **HAUI Display** within seconds instead of after the 20-minute timeout. Home Assistant also checks a TFT URL first and refuses a `404`, a server that ignores range requests or an oversized file before the panel is sent off to download it ([Troubleshooting](docs/user/troubleshooting.md#tft-upload-failures)).
